utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 6, I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Misetic, are you ready to continue your cross-examination? Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President and Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, in your statement, you indicated that you did not believe -- I'm sorry, you said, "I did not expect there would be an attack on Knin." That is at paragraph 11 of your statement. However, you also indicated that you had moved your family to Belgrade on the 30th of July, and that would include your wife and your children. Without mentioning any names --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would be helpful if the witness could be given a copy of his statement in order that he can see the context in which these comments are made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have a copy for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He had the B/C/S copy yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yesterday, yes, and I think it was provided by you, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would have another spare copy then. Meanwhile, I believe we can continue because you are more or less quoting from his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Without mentioning names, how many other family members left on or about the 30th of July?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, wouldn't it be wise to specify whether how many people left from the city of Knin, from the whole of the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Also try to establish what the basis of knowledge of this witness is, if it goes beyond his own street.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this question: Did any people leave with your family that you know of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You have to answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please speak, because if you nod, this is not audible on the transcript. Mr. Misetic, do I understand your question well that you were asking the witness how many families left with his family before the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the shelling started?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Before the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hadn't even started answering. I'm just indicating that I understand your question. Prior to the 4th of August, what I can tell you is that some of the population, a rather small part of the population, in fact, several per cent perhaps, had left Knin. That was the Sunday before the Monday that the Operation Storm began. The bus had arrived from Belgrade, and I know that the mood in the town was rather sullen. In the north of the municipality, there is a place called Strmica near Knin, which had been shelled already. Most of the people who were there had left Strmica by this time and had arrived in Knin. Since my wife hails from the area, members of her family, too, who lived in that area came over, and they were now in my flat. That morning, that Sunday morning, four or five days before Operation Storm, I found out about the bus, and members of my wife's family were adamant that they would leave for Belgrade to stay with their relatives there. They then tried to talk me into allowing my wife, with our two children, to leave as well. I didn't feel that was absolutely necessary. I didn't think that worse would come to worse. Unfortunately, I was proven wrong and they were proven right. They got onto a bus. Tickets had been sold for about between 150 and 200 people, and 100 got on eventually. I was there to see that bus off along with a number of other people. That was the last bus, and it is easy to realise that a single bus would not do in terms of evacuating the entire population. Therefore, there were some private vehicles that were being used as well, several per cent. I can only assume, but I think between 5 and 10 per cent of the overall population left Knin and everybody else remain. That would be as much as I know. I know the day the bus left there was a rally outside the railway station, and the patriarch Pavle was there, too. He gave a speech; and as he was given this speech in the evening hours, the bus was leaving Knin. Now you're asking me about my expectations, why did I not see Operation Storm coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't ask that. In your statement, you stated that, "They would remain in Belgrade until the danger passed." I'm sorry, let me read you the whole sentence. "It was intended that they would remain in Belgrade until the danger passed." What danger were you talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never thought that the danger would be that tragic. I did feel that there would be some sort of operations, but I thought there would be a peaceful resolution to that soon because I never thought that the entire population of Knin would be made to leave. I was lucky, though, because my family did not have to go through the same things that I eventually had to go through. I say "danger" because danger was in the air. Intuitively, I realised that the danger would not be that tragic, maybe because I'd never been involved in a war before. I had no idea what shelling meant. This was the first time I ever experienced anything like that. Those who had prior experience of things such as those were maybe still in time to send their families away. In my case, it was quite accidental. I do have to say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, that Mr. Martic had declared a state of war on the 28th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of that. I wasn't even aware of the decision that he apparently took for all those who weren't involved in the fighting to leave Knin, because by the time the decision was taken, I had already made up my mind. I suppose the decision was taken on the afternoon of the 4th, by which time I was in a village near Knin on the road to Srb. A column of vehicles was moving along that road, and that column involved almost everybody leaving the Serbia Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We'll get back to this topic in a moment, sir, but I also want to talk to you about the video that was shown yesterday in court. You indicated that the video had been given to you sometime around a year after you had arrived in Belgrade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it could be or could have been a year later that I was given the footage. This officer who handed that over to me told me that he had taken some footage, that he had a recording of that. At first, I wasn't even interested, and then he gave me the footage. I realised when I watched it the same things that you can see for yourselves yesterday as were watching it. Secondly, as I said, the footage had been shown previously on a variety of TV shows, especially on RTS, because it was meant to be used for the purposes of some documentary or something, a documentary film festival or whatever they were organising.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And just to clarify, you arrived in Belgrade in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, August; the 5th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So you would have received this video sometime in 1996, maybe 1997?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think late 1996 or 1997. I assumed the footage indicates the year that it was made. That's my assumption. The year must be indicated. It was made during Operation Storm. I'm not sure when they edited the footage and then pieced it together, but I think there's an indication of the year it was made somewhere rather on that video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking for when the year the video was made. I'm asking, just so we're clear, the year you received a copy of the video.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can tell, about a year after Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You then indicated that, in anticipation of your witness statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, you had a copy of the video made onto a DVD by the Veritas organisation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I gave it to them to do; and as I observed, they placed their own name there, "Veritas." But, actually, the only thing that they provided at the time was technical assistance. They made a copy of the tape, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Between the time you received the video, approximately a year after you arrived in Belgrade, until your appearance in court yesterday, do you know of any changes to the audio or video that was shown in court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no changes were made. You can find the same footage elsewhere as well. This is just one copy of it. I suppose there must be dozens or hundreds of it floating around. This is just one of those copies, and the only distinction is this one actually displays the name of the organisation, Veritas, simply because they produced the copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir -- strike that. In your discussions with the filmmaker, who I believe you indicated yesterday was Colonel Nestorovic, did Colonel Nestorovic indicate to you that there was unedited footage of the scenes we saw yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he gave me the footage, the footage was clearly based on the recordings that he had done in Knin. He put this together and that was what I got. He was preparing for some sort of a festival, and it had been aired on RTS. The film had been made public some time ago -- some time before. I simply happened to be there when The Hague investigator was also present, and this gave me a chance to hand the material over to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that the Office of the Prosecutor has the unedited video that was originally shot on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that the audio from the original video has been distorted in the video that you presented in court yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me show you a comparison of the original video that was produced to the Defence by the Office of the Prosecutor versus the video you presented in court. You will recall the scene of women and children running across the street under an air raid siren, and I'll let you compare the one video that was produced by the Prosecution to the Defence and then the video you presented in court yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, you have referred several times to the audio as well. The audio is not in evidence, at least is not being ignored by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm not talking about the voiceover. I'm talking about the actual sound what was happening in Knin, and I believe, Your Honour, you did indicate that you were able to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, the sound of the shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, before we continue, these two extracts, are they uploaded in e-court, because would they need a number?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The video you've seen is uploaded -- this extract is uploaded in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I have not loaded the entire raw footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. I do understand that we saw part of what we saw yesterday, and we saw a different version of the same picture but different sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you'd like to have this in evidence, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it needs a number. Now, how did you -- are these two separate items, or is it one item prepared?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's one video, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's one video which contains a portion of what we saw yesterday, and added to that the new version of that same portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I wish to be clear so there's no misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The video you just saw is in one video that we prepared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, a compilation of the two. One we've seen already and the together is one. Now, what is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me make sure we're on the same page here. But they come from two separate videos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. Do you have a number for Madam Registrar of what was just played, your 65 ter number or the D numbers as you call them?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's our 65 ter number 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: For us. We don't have is a -- we just need an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it clear what was played so you can assign an exhibit number to it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Not really right now but I'll work it out with the case manager with the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will already assign a number for it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit D13, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D13, marked for identification, for the time being and then the original number will be given to Madam Registrar. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, do you know who added the siren to the video you played yesterday? Are you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, in your question, it is implied that the siren was added and not the birds were added. Would you please be clear on that? We have two versions, two different versions. Whether the siren was there and has been removed and replaced by birds, or whether there were birds replaced by a siren is not yet established, so you should not imply this in your question which could lead to confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you know who would have been responsible for the sound in the video you played yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I can tell. I suppose the original tape that I handed over for a copy to be made should be the copy that arrived here, in addition to which I think the original tape must still be available. I could have it sent to you personally, if that means anything, so that you can cross-reference it to your tapes. It was Veritas, was it not? I think not, because the only thing they had to do was make a copy of that tape. I don't think they actually had the equipment to introduce any new editing moves or to change the original footing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It appears that the witness has no knowledge on what has been done, so let's stop speculating. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And there's one additional clip, Your Honour, that I'd like to show the witness. This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that then also a separate footage consisting of two --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's correct. In the break, we will add the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, that would then be D14, I take it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar, and also marked for identification for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you mind to play it once again, so I'm better able to see it - it's very short - and so to better understand where the differences are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And at the end of the video, Madam Registrar, if you could keep the picture up, because I'd like the witness to identify, if he can, the location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sir, in this video, you see a gentleman walking --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sir, in this video, you see a gentleman in a uniform walking in the background. Can you identify that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to admit -- is there a person behind this car? Is it the gentleman that we saw in that recording yesterday, Nestorovic? Again, I really wasn't paying attention to that because I hadn't realised you'd be asking me about it. But I do notice a person there behind, and this person might be Colonel Nestorovic, the one behind the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. That is the question. I wanted to know if you could identify if that is Colonel Nestorovic in the background.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If perhaps we could make the image a bit clearer, then perhaps I might be certain about that. As it is now, I'm merely speculating.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will play it back a few seconds for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And I have two questions on the scene, so if you could pay attention to the first question. The first question, what I've just asked you, is if you can identify the person in the video. The second question is if you can identify the building in the background of this video, so that the Court can be aware of where the hole is in this video that is shown at the beginning of the clip.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That person might be the director, the Director Nestorovic. But to tell you the truth, the location after 12 years I would find it hard to define where it is, because it was -- it had sustained quite a lot of damage in relation to the way I knew it before the shelling. So I couldn't really be specific about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Were you familiar with how the headquarters of the army of the Republika Srpska Krajina looked on the 3rd of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise whether that is the back of the army of the RSK headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you've just shown me, whether this is the army hall in Knin, the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I want to be clear here. Is this the parking lot behind the army hall that you mentioned yesterday in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might be the parking lot based on what we saw yesterday where the shells fell next to the army hall. It might be the location that they recorded, and that might be reflected in this recording. That would be next to the army hall in Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, I'd like to have full clarity here. Witness 6, earlier you said, "I find it hard to define where it is, because it had sustained quite a lot of damage in relation to the way I knew it before the shelling." When you said that, what location were you referring to at that moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I was referring to the location that I saw on this video footage, because things don't look the way I recall them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tell us what --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tell us what, in your view, we saw only the video. Which building did we see? I mean, name it if you can, because you say, "It's different from how I knew it," which gives the impression that you know what premises you're talking about. Tell us what you had in mind when you said that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday -- well, on the basis of what we saw yesterday, the images of shelling, we indicated on a photograph that a building had been hit and that there was a fire burning near the city centre. I have to admit that now this image is not clear enough for me to be able to define what building that is. I cannot recognise this place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I want to stop you here. I'm not talking about yesterday. I'm talking about today. You look at the footage you saw today, that is the place where a lot of cars can be seen, and you said, "Well, things have changed; therefore, I have some difficulties in locating it. It is not as I used to know it." What location did you have in mind at that moment? Was it the local grocery store? Was it a police station? Was it a hospital? What did you have in mind? I'd like to have of a direct answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence counsel asked me whether this was next to the army hall in Knin, and then I intuitively thought that it might be next -- somewhere next to the army hall. But at this moment, I cannot give you a decisive, certain answer as to whether this was next to the army hall, because after 12 years, this has faded in my mind. I didn't go to that area much after the war, so I cannot claim that this was really the location that is being put to me by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 6, before you were asked if it was the army hall, you gave the answer I just read out to you. That was before one question has been put to you. You said, and I'll repeat it, "I would find it hard to define where it was because it had sustained quite a lot of damage in relation to the way I knew it before the shelling. So I couldn't really be specific about that." What were you referring to as "it"? What had sustained quite a lot of damage? This was before any question about the army hall was put to you. What did you refer to at that moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, on this footage, I saw that there was damage to the shops, that there was a lot of broken glass on the floor, we saw the broken branches --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 6, I'm not talking about the broken glass. I am talking about the location where you see the cars, that parking lot. What did you have in mind if you said you had difficulties to locate it? Was that in relation to the parking lot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, what I meant was that from where I am now, I cannot define the exact location of this parking lot. I admit that I cannot recall whether this is the location next to the army hall. If I were in Knin, I would then be able to look at it, see what it looks like, and be more specific about the location; but from where I sit here, as much as I'm trying to recall this location, I cannot now claim that I really know where this location was, where this parking lot was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you saw, did it look like what you remember was the parking lot of that location, that is, the army hall? Does it look similar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can recall -- or, rather, I don't recall that there was the staircase there at the parking lot next to the army hall. I assumed that there were several similar locations in Knin. And on the basis of the footage you've just shown me, I would not be able to determine whether this was, indeed, next to the army hall, because right across the street from it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 6, I didn't ask you to identify it. My last question was whether it looked similar to. Does it or does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to admit that this doesn't look like the parking lot at the army hall building. It doesn't look similar to that, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, based on at that question, I'd like to ask the witness two follow-up questions. If you could look at the video, and we've paused it, my foundational question, Your Honour, is this:

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with what police vehicles looked like in Knin prior to the 4th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I am familiar with it. They might look like the vehicles depicted here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall what colour licence plates police vehicles had in Knin prior to the 4th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I don't know that. I never actually looked at the licence plates. I never paid any attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If you could look at the next clip, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that need a separate number?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be D15 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: -- marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification. Could we start it? Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That vehicle you see there on the right there, sir, does that look like a police car, the type of police car you would have seen in Knin prior to the 4th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It does look like a police car. That's the kind of cars that the police in Knin had.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Misetic, did I see something different, or did I see the same as I saw in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's the same video. We just stopped it, so that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then it would not need a new number. Then the number D15 will be vacated. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, yesterday, you were asked a series of questions by the Presiding Judge regarding Zastava Films and Colonel Nestorovic, so I'd like to ask you a couple of questions about his role. Zastava Films was the film production company of the Yugoslav national army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that Zastava Film was being used -- strike the word "used." Are you aware that Zastava Film was being utilized by the army of the Republika Srpska Krajina in the weeks and months before Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. They were present in Knin. That's what I can tell you. That's what I do know. They followed a military exercise that had been going on in Slunj. I think it was for St. Vitus's Day, and they were in Knin on that day by accident. That's what I think, by accident. They were in a position to record everything that happened on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have disclosed last night a document which has not been loaded in e-court yet, but it is an internal of the army RSK document indicating precisely what the witness says regarding the video recording of a military exercise in June. And in the document that we've disclosed to the Prosecution - actually, it was given to us by the Prosecution and disclosed - we indicated we wished to use it. In the document, internal RSK document, it says that the Zastava Film company will make this production for the use by the military.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, is this -- or Mr. Margetts, is this a matter that is challenged or would you agree that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: We have no challenge to that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No challenge to that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we need it in evidence, or is it - let me just have a look at it - or is it agreed that this --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Just for clarity, we have no challenge to the admission of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we're not talking about any agreement on the content of whether it's true or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then it's up to you to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is not yet uploaded, so I take it that your case manager will deal with Madam Registrar as soon as it has been uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the number to be assigned to it is, I take it, the vacated number, D15, marked for -- no, not marked for identification. There's no objection against it, so it could be an exhibit right away. Admitted into evidence, D15.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, there's another matter. Please proceed and I'll find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, yesterday, the Presiding Judge asked you a question about Colonel Nestorovic's role and whether he was acting in a military capacity, and the transcript reference is page 892, lines 21 to 22. In your response, you said: "He was a colonel by rank, but he wasn't into the military. What he was into, to the extent that I could judge, was culture." Do you recall that testimony yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what you mean when you say he was not in the army. If he held the rank of a colonel, that means he was in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm simply repeating what you said yesterday, and I'm asking you -- again, your quote yesterday was: "He was a colonel by rank, but he wasn't into the military. What he was into, to the extent that I could judge, was culture." That was your quote -- your statement yesterday; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, you're right. If I may just clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you some questions. Let me --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've asked me this question, if I can be allowed to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can add whatever you'd like to at the end of it; but, at this moment, you should listen to the questions put to you by Mr. Misetic. Then, Mr. Misetic, may I take it that you will indicate when we're leaving this subject, and then the witness will have an opportunity to further add. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Colonel Nestorovic was working for the film production company of the Yugoslav army. You recognise that; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He was in military uniform filming on the 4th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was in a military uniform, and he was recording things on the 4th of August. That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to dispute that Colonel Nestorovic was exercising a military function on the 4th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't understand what you're asking me, "exercising." He was filming things as he had been doing in the previous days for Zastava Film; and on that day, he recorded footage. I don't know whether it was for the purpose of Zastava Film or whether that was for his personal use and then he went on to make a movie out of that. But we can see here that it says "Zastava Film," so this film was actually produced by Zastava Film. When I said that he was into culture, he told me that within the military, he was dealing with culture, that he was a director, and that he directed this film. That's all I know about him. I didn't really socialise with him so that I could be able to give you more details about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So we're in agreement that, although you say he was dealing with culture, it was culture within the context of the military; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, because the army produced films. You know that Zastava Film was a production company and that they produced education -- educational materials for the army. They produced those films, and he worked in Zastava Film for the army as a director.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, in some of your answers to my most recent questions, you've said -- you indicated that you've had conversations with Colonel Nestorovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had some conversations with him to the effect that I met him on that day when this footage was made. I was dealing with culture myself, and I wanted to use him to do some recordings that would -- that I could use for my job, for what I was doing, to make some recordings of the Knin fortress and so on. So that's how I actually came to meet him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In the course of your conversations, you also had conversations about his filming on the 4th of August, 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't talk to him. I had talked to him in days before. On that day, I did not see him. I did not discuss the recordings on the 4th because I didn't know that this would happen on the 4th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think you misunderstood the question. I'm asking you in subsequent conversations, in the months and years after Operation Storm, did you have conversations with Colonel Nestorovic about his filming the events of the 4th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the subsequent conversations, actually, I met with him once or twice when he handed over the film to me. He had told me that he had something for me. He handed over the film to me, telling me how the film came to be made, and the film itself speaks for itself. Because of the contacts that we had had, he felt an obligation to call me and to tell me that he had some footage, and then he handed the footage over it me. But I did not remain in contact with him, so we didn't have many occasions to meet and to socialise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In your conversations with Colonel Nestorovic, who is now deceased; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he is not deceased. He's retired. I assume that he left Belgrade and that he lives in Serbian hinterland somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. In your conversations with Colonel Nestorovic, did he ever tell you that he was able to film from different locations on the 4th because the UN force in Knin had loaned him an armoured vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the first that I hear of those forces loaning him an armoured vehicle. He told me that he filmed various locations as he moved around the town with his cameraman called Zubovic. He even climbed up onto the Knin fortress, and you can see that some broad sweeps were filmed from up there. You can see that he started making his recordings right in the early morning when the attack started. He went all the way up to the Knin hospital. As far as I know, from what he told me, he simply walked around the town. That's how he made all those recordings. He did not use any vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to ask you the following question: On the 4th of August, was there smoke coming from the area of the Tvik factory in Knin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to note that the air in the whole of the town was different than it usually was. I can't tell why that was. Maybe because of all the roofs that had been hit. There was some red plumes of smoke all over the town. There was a weird atmosphere in the air, and I think that this was something that you could perceive as you breathed. There was this strange air in the town, and I think that you could not see the sun because of everything that was in the air. There was -- there were those clouds rising up all over the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Misetic did not invite you to describe the totality of the air in the city. His question simply was whether there was smoke coming from the area of the Tvik factory. Could you please focus your answer on that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can give my answer, and that is that clouds were rising up as I moved around the town. As I explained yesterday, I was able to see that there were clouds of smoke rising up above Tvik factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Your Honours, we've prepared a Power Point presentation of the video. It's in e-court, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It is number 16 on our list which is 1D11-06-06.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that would be D16, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I have already asked about the comparative videos, is there is any objection against admission of those?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. There is no objection against the admission of the comparative videos. We would only say this, that the second video is also on our 65 ter list and we had intended to introduce that in evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then you can use that at a later stage, since it is already admitted as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think, as I understand, the Defence movement for admission, it's for the portions of the video that they've selected, rather than the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you'd say the whole of it you had on your list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: So we would say that we had the whole of the video on the list, and we would come back to it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will see whether there is any need to assign a new number to that when you want to introduce that. For the time being, Madam Registrar, the two comparative videos which are, I think, 13 and 14, if I'm correct, are admitted into evidence. Please proceed with the Power Point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't have the exhibit on my screen, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Neither do I.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sorry. It's just, Madam Registrar, 1D11.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me note, first, the green pin, there in the middle, does that mark the location of the Tvik factory in Knin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's where the Tvik factory was in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask, Your Honours. We now have the different locations from which Colonel Nestorovic filmed, and we can take the Trial Chamber in the video to each location. But our objective is to show the Court that Colonel Nestorovic shot the spoke from the Tvik factory from each of these different angles, and it creates the appearance that there is smoke coming from different buildings. If the court wishes, I can take you through each scene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's not in my memory any more the details of every plume of smoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, therefore, please guide us through it and ask the witness -- I don't know whether the witness can add anything to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, yesterday, he was used by the Prosecution, Your Honour, to identify smoke coming from various areas, so I would like to put questions to him and to say: Is this the direction toward the Tvik factory?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: For the transcript, Your Honour, we are now going to 9:06 in the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's actually on 9:08 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's actually now 9:08 on the video that I'm looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, the flames and the smoke that we see in this picture, is that the area of the Tvik factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell, based on what I know about the location of the cameraman and Colonel Nestorovic -- well, I can't. I can't really tell you where the smoke is coming from here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The picture seems of such a darkness that I wonder whether it's wise to insist on obtaining further evidence on --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I can move on then, and through a further witness try to establish --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We're going now to 9:21 in the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this location in the town of Knin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recognise anything at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Next, we'll move to 10:48.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do recognise this location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You do recognise this location. Is the Tvik factory behind this location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Agroprevreda. It's in front of the factory, and the factory's right behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: 11:01 is the next clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this location in Knin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can tell, this is the bridge over the rail tracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And do you know what is to the left of the bridge over the railway tracks in Knin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be Tvik, the factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour -- thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The next clip is 12:23.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this location in Knin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is in the north of Knin, and these are the buildings that we marked yesterday, across the way from the Veljko Vlahovic elementary school building. It is the same neighbourhood as Agroprevreda and the Tvik factory. These buildings are behind those locations that I've just specified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Where is the Tvik factory in relation to the buildings that we see here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is behind these buildings where you can see the smoke rising.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: 12:44 is the next clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Again, for the transcript, there's a Slight correction. It is 12:46 in the video that's being presented in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this location in Knin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the railway station.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us where the Tvik factory is in relation to this picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it's precisely where you can see the smoke rising.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The next is at 13 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this location in Knin, Witness 6?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same place you showed me a while ago. The angle was different though. This is the bridge over the railway tracks and the plume of smoke rising from where the Tvik factory should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And 13:05, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe you identified this -- or, yesterday, we discussed this clip. But the smoke in the background there, where is that coming from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What we're looking at is two different places from which the smoke is coming: One is to the left of the Tvik factory and the other is to the right. There are two separate locations that were shelled and that caught fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to turn next to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, next, we'd like to turn to 1D11-0607.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would be, Madam Registrar, number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D17, marked for identification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any objections against the Power Point presentation?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise. Let me go back to that exhibit just so I can ask --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sorry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness, you've now looked at the videos. Does this presentation accurately reflect the different locations from which the video of the Tvik factory burning was shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was recorded as a number of different locations, and then all the way to those buildings near the school building in the northern sector of Knin. So this was the route that they followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And you're saying that your information is that Colonel Nestorovic walked throughout the entire area on this map from which we see the different locations that filming took place?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness's evidence on the record is that he did recognise some of the locations. Accordingly, I think, if there is going to be a representation of the witness's evidence, it needs to reflect which locations he recognised and which locations he didn't recognise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe there were two locations that he did not recognise, Your Honour, and we will amend the exhibit for this witness. I'll submit one to counsel, and we can go over it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That being clarified, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now I'd like to turn to the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But before doing so, with great interest, of course, I listened to the answers of the witness. If I see a picture being shot with a camera, knowing that cameras can zoom in, can zoom out, can do all kind of things, shouldn't we first ask the witness: Were you present when these pictures were shot by Mr. Nestorovic? Did you follow him on his trip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I didn't even see him that day. I have no idea what he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you say that the locations, as marked on this picture, are the locations from where the pictures were shot? It's not of your own observation, but it's just on the basis of the footage that you saw that you confirm that these are the places; is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, based on what I saw, because as I said, I was not with Colonel Nestorovic that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Even if I would be very familiar with Knin, Mr. Misetic, I wonder how I ever could say it was at this distance. Direction, fine; altitude, higher, lower, fine; but distance?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't think I was talking about distance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, locations from where the pictures were shot. That means the distance to the Tvik factory, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I can imagine that you say it was from a higher point of view, from a lower point of view; direction, fine. But if I shoot a picture you now, how could you know that it was five metres or whether I'm one metre further back or one metre further. So you're asking the witness something, at least in my view, but please correct me if I'm wrong, he could not possibly infer from which angle --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] I understand, Your Honour but I'm only interested in the angle, not the location it was shot at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the angle. If you say it's angle and that's what you ask the witness to confirm, then I'm fine with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But locations, I'm not fine with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I was just interested in the angle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The next page, please. In light of your last comment, Your Honour, I'm not sure how interested you'll be in this, but this slide is intended to show you the images we've just shown, where the angle would have come from each image. It's intended it show how the camera crew would have travelled to shoot all these locations. Because in the original video, if you note the minute markings on the video, you'll see that the film develops in a temporal order on the video, and you can follow exactly the path that's taken to shoot it. Our intention is only to show not the -- I'm not interested in proving where the cameramen were, just to show the comparison with the next picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then again, I take this is on the basis of an assumption that the timing on the video corresponds with the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Angles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the timing of the original chronology, which, as far as I am concerned, is not yet established, neither is it established --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I do not know what the sequence in the original film is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were, I take it, paying some attention to editing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted to show the next slide, and you'll see the editing. This is the original which we would present and I guess we will introduce it when the Prosecution introduces through its 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the raw material you're now talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In fact, it's 65 ter number 3759, which is the video that we intended to introduce at some stage in the proceeding. It seems, since we're analysing these images in this detail, that we -- it would be appropriate to move the admission of that video now in the context of this witnesses evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to the parties whether they think this is the appropriate moment to introduce that material, but we're now talking about -- because I see that on this picture, there are times indicated, and that's on the raw material. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this challenged in any way?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do challenge that image. We're not entirely sure how helpful this image is, and we certainly think that it would probably be beneficial if we were able to discuss with the Defence the video introduced and this video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're invited to do so; but at this moment, the Defence is working on the basis that the times, as indicated on this picture, are times taken from the original raw material, and I take it then it's the time from the camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Right. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's, therefore, a different time from the times we saw on the footage, where the time indicates where in time in this edited footage we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whereas, here we are talking about real time on the raw material apparently coming from the camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me propose this. If we could go to the next page. I just want to go to the next page, and we will -- just so the Court under stands what we're doing. But I will talk to counsel during the break and then we'll work out how we want to -- how we wish to do this comparison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At least we now know on the basis of what assumption you are presenting this to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct. This next slide, it was intended to compare the two and then to show, in the film that you saw yesterday, the sequencing of how things were represented and images were ordered does not follow how a logical path through Knin would have taken place. Again, I will work with counsel during the break and see if we can't work out an agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So what you present in evidence is two reconstructions --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- one on the basis of the timing in the original raw material, the other one on the basis of the timing as we found it in the edited version of this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I could inquire, Your Honour, what does the Chamber intend to take a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Usually at 10.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, I'd like to take you through some of the images that you identified yesterday from the video that we were looking at, and one was image -- or point E that you identified. This was identified by the Prosecution, point E, location of damaged buildings depicted at counter times 12:24:87 and 12:28:83.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I guess these images are not in e-court yet, just the slides, Your Honour, that we were using yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The slides of yesterday, no, they were not, because I think we considered this just reproduced and was material that would assist us in viewing the images we had seen already on the video. So, therefore, these have not been given exhibit numbers. If you need them, please tell us; otherwise, just refer to them by the timing of the video as we did yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Then if we could -- this is 12:24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could there be placed again on the ELMO as they were yesterday, or do we see them now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm actually going to use the video, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. Then we leave it as this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, you were asked to identify where this location is yesterday, and you marked that location as "point E." Can you tell us where the Senjak military barracks is in relation to that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Senjak military barracks was behind these buildings. I think this is a neighbourhood that people locally referred to as the 3rd of December. So the Senjak barracks was right behind these roofs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know if Milan Martic lived in the general area of these houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in these buildings but nearby, at least as far as I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to 13:07 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is now 13:07.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is what you identified as "F" on the map yesterday. Do you -- where is the army hall in relation to the burning house here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army hall was sort of to the north at a distance of about 50 metres from this house, or thereabouts. What you can see in the foreground is the old Knin secondary school. That is the middle of the town, the centre of town; and, right behind, you can see the railway station and the smoke over it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if we could call up 1D11-0610.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, is that a close-up picture of the house that you marked as point F on the map yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see exactly what it is right now. Right here, in this corner, this passage between the two houses, I know that place really well because my manager used to live there. Across the way is the health station attached to the railway station; and then you can see a private home there that was hit, and I think the Dinara Hotel is nearby. That's the other site. It's right above. You can't actually see it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, Madam Registrar, and the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. Your Honour, I think there was something missed that the witness said about the military facility being located nearby. It was missed in the translation in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could please confer with Mr. Misetic so that he knows which question he should put again to the witness, so that we can hear the complete answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In answering the last question, Your Honour, I'm sorry, the witness had mentioned is something about the military barracks in B/C/S being just outside of where this picture was, and it did not get caught in the translation into the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask the witness again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you please ask that again. Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you can follow the original language and that something is missing. Nevertheless, you're invited not to explain what's wrong, but to point at a translation issue and ask for it to be repeated, rather than to tell everyone what the answer was, which could have an effect which I am certain you did not intend --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but which could have a certain effect --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which I'd like to avoid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, in your prior your answer, could you repeat your prior answer with respect to military barracks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can say is that the building on fire, where we can see the fire, this is at a distance of about 100 or 200 metres, not from the barracks, but from the army hall, because that was the army hall in Knin and the barracks was up north. This is further south. This is not where the barracks was. This was the army hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to page 3 of this exhibit, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, does the area with the circle mark the house that was shelled on the 4th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The area that is marked with a -- go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm actually quite certain about that because I went to that school, which is right next to the house that was shelled. Therefore, I'm quite familiar with this part of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, to the left there, in the area marked rectangularly, is that the complex the Main Staff of the army of Srpska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know this rectangle that I can see is quite large, but there is an arrow there coming from above, and that would roughly be consistent with the place where -- well, I can't be quite specific. If I could, I would show you where the army hall might be, but I can't tell you here because the rectangle is actually quite large, and I can't place the army hall there. Maybe if I can use the ELMO and if you want me to show you there, I could be more specific. It is certainly an at a distance of about 100 metres, say, in relation to the building that was shelled that we were looking at a while ago, perhaps even less, maybe 70 to 80 metres in relation to this circle that we can see here, and then within this rectangle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't know if the Court wishes to break now, but I have some follow-up questions on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If that would take more than just one or two minutes, then we will have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, one or two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, this series of photographs has not been assigned a number yet. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be D18, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have we had the whole of the series yet or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think there's one more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's one more, then we will wait to hear if there's any objection after we have seen the whole of the series.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have a break now, Witness 6, and we will resume at 11.00. Could you give us an indication of how much more time you need, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think I can hopefully wrap up in about an hour, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, yesterday, you will recall you marked for identification on your map point G, and I'll pull the video so you can refer to the scene. I'm referring now to that smoke in the background there. Do you recall testifying about the location of that smoke yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that your testimony, in marking this location, was that the smoke was coming from a residential area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this still, we can see two plumes of smoke rising in two different locations. The one closer to us is in the town self near the railway station -- in front of the railway station towards the fortress. And the other one that you can see further off, that's behind Agroprevreda. Right next to it, there's the Tvik factory. But as far as this plume of smoke, as far as I can tell, that is a residential area. There are private moments there, and Senjak, the military barracks, is also nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we can assist the Trial Chamber, Witness 6, I will pull up --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, 1D11-0591.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the Senjak barracks, Witness 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That exhibit will be assigned what number, or is it one of the series?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It needs a new number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It needs a new number, because I think you said we went through the series apart from one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. We had a discussion during the break, Your Honour, and we will not tender the last exhibit. I am assuming that's what we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We're looking at a series of photographs, isn't it, where you said, I think, we have seen three out of four.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is a new exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is a new exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what will happen to the series, because we waited for you to show the last one, the fourth in line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had a discussion about the series and the rationale for that presentation and representation of the videos. The parties have come to some substantial agreement with regard to the videos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will refrain from any further questions. Madam Registrar, this 1D11-0591 would have what exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will have D18, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Page 2, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, you mentioned, in your last answer, the Senjak military barracks. Can you tell the Trial Chamber where on this map the Senjak military barracks is located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would need another building to be pointed out to me, because I cannot see this on this image. I was never in a position to look at a map of this sort, so I would need some assistance to be able to point to Senjak. As it is, I'm unable to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, I believe the map that you marked yesterday is also an aerial photograph. When you marked the map for the Prosecution, I believe it was -- you were able to mark the residential location. Perhaps if we look --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I marked it as being across the road from the Tvik factory. The area marked with G would be the residential area, and the Senjak is somewhere nearby. It is just before this area marked with G.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So the -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, would it be an idea that we use the technical facilities of marking on these kind of maps that would then have another copy which could be marked for the witness, or even this one to be marked by the witness? The only important thing is it cannot be zoomed in and out any more once the marking has started; but if the witness says this is before this or before that, then of course the Chamber is lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, with the assistance of the usher, we could do some markings. At the same time, I'm a bit concerning about you marking "G" on a map which is not fully corresponding with what yesterday was marked as G, because only the right hand portion of G is what is in the G circle of yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps could we mark this map, then, nevertheless, if he can identify where the military barracks is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you want, but then we only have the marked map. But that's fine as far as I'm concerned. Mr. Usher, could you please. Could we also -- what colours do we have available? Red, blue. Shall we take that, as more or less as a standard, marking in red in the future will be marking on the request of the Prosecution and marking in blue would be the marking on the request of the Defence. Mr. Usher, could you give the blue pen to the witness. The witness should not start marking unless he knows exactly what he's invited to mark. If so, would you first carefully listen to Mr. Misetic before you start marking. Mr. Misetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, if I may. Would I like to make a correction of the transcript. This document will be D19 instead of D18.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, could you please circle the area --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to avoid any confusion, that's 1D11-0592, which has now received this new exhibit number. I do understand that, in the end, 91 and 92 is the same exhibit. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness, 6, could you please circle the area on this map that is the Senjak military barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's this area here. I think that's the area behind the buildings that we were able to see and that we marked. But the Senjak military barracks did not serve that function. Some new premises, some new buildings were built there. That was not the army that was there. That was just some new buildings that were built during the war. I think that the Senjak military barracks area would correspond with this area that I marked as "G" here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Could you -- could you identify on this map, with a number 1, the area that you believe -- you believe is the area that was hit by shells and that you identified as mark "G" yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this map that I see in front of me?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] So should I put in "1" here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me take you to the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is going to be minute mark 10:13 of the video that was presented in court yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, are we already at a point where we could save the marked exhibits, or do you need still further marking because we have then a problem, because it will disappear from the screen. So you see what the problem is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marking is a process which starts and ends, and so we have to store this one, and we cannot do another marking on the same one. Then we should retrieve this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, let my say this: I believe, when the witness sees the video, he may make different markings. So I don't mind that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So this one is not to be saved at this moment. It's just the original, that's 0591, which unmarked is there, and you might invite him to do another marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then just for the record, so that it's there, that the witness marked on this picture in the right square, to say, marked with a letter "G," he circled around this letter G and marked a 1 in blue on this map. But it will not be saved at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to eliminate any confusion regarding the colourings to be used, is it that the Defence witnesses are to use red or just witnesses when they're being questioned by the Defence are to use red?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll think about this very useful question and then give you further guidance. Mr. Kuzmanovic, I can tell you already the following: The importance of the difference in colours is that, if a witness marks on behalf of one party and then add some marking on the request of another party, then at the end we find a picture with a lot of markings on it, and we do not know any more which marking was made by whom.
