So, therefore, I would say it's not a matter of Defence or Prosecution witnesses, but rather on who's request the markings were made.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, do you see the video in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that would be facing the fortress, more or less. I think this was taken from an area close to the Tvik factory, because this might be the view of the fortress from that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That wall that you see there, is that a wall that surrounded the Senjak military barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might be. That is the position, and you might say that it actually went around the Senjak barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could play the video slowly until -- until 10:24.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you see the fire in the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This might be, yes. I think that this was one of the new buildings that were built there at Senjak. That's the building that was hit there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's a building that was part of Senjak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, part of Senjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is this building close to the area that you marked as "G" on the map yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume. Actually, now that I'm looking at this film, and having in mind the map that we saw yesterday, I think that this building was a little bit away from the area that we marked. It was closer to the town. The one that we marked yesterday was a little bit away. I was unable to determine that yesterday, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, we can go back --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- now I can determine that this is the area of the Senjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, then I'd like to go back to 13:33 of the -- of this same video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, the burning building that was part of Senjak, is that in the general vicinity of the smoke that we see in the background of this clip?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume that what we saw a little while ago might be the plume of smoke rising from that very same location, and that that is the building that was hit that we have seen just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for my understanding, earlier a wall was shown, and you testified that this the wall or the kind of wall that surrounded Senjak. Now, from where that picture was taken, was that inside or was that just outside the Senjak complex?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The footage was taken outside of the wall, the wall of the Senjak compound. What is shown here is from further away, but I assume that it might be showing the area that we saw before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did I then also understand well that the fire we saw, which was when the camera panned to left, is still outside the Senjak complex?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assumed it was inside the Senjak compound. When the camera is switched on, when it starts to move, we can see that the burning building is inside the fenced-in area; but after all, you can check that on the spot because the remains of that building still stand in Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you please look at your screen where we have this original picture looking in the direction of the fortress. You see there's a wall consisting of what seems to be some kind of concrete, or whatever other material, with some buildings of which only the roofs are visible to the right of that wall. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, are those buildings where we can only see the roofs, are they inside or outside the Senjak complex?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are inside the complex, as far as I'm able to ascertain, looking from this side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then when the camera pans to the left and shows the picture of a burning structure, then my inference would be that that would be outside the Senjak complex as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the best thing to do would be to look at the recording and to see, because I'm unable to determine that there here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have the possibility to play that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the basis of this, I'm unable to determine whether it was inside or outside, because Senjak was walled in on all four sides by that wall that we saw. So I can't tell from which side this recording was taken. I assume it was inside Senjak, because that building that was set on fire was inside the Senjak compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there anyway the parties could agree on this, because the witness is to some extent confusing me, unless that wall goes in unexpected --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I can go back with the consent of the Court and leeway from my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The only thing I want to know is whether we looked at a picture of a structure, apparently it looks like a house, burning inside or outside that complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will make an offer of proof, Your Honour, that it's not a house. It's actually a depot, and it is outside the complex itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We hardly can see anything from that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's why I was using the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if there's any objection against the Chamber understanding, this was outside the Senjak complex, whatever it might have been, then I'd like to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, our understanding is consistent with Your Honour's understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we don't need to bother the witness with it any more. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Again, can we have the Exhibit D19 back on the screen. With a little --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you like to have the unmarked or marked version on the screen at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Unmarked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unmarked. Is there a possibility, Madam Registrar, to have the unmarked version? It's even possible to -- yes. Mr. Usher, could you please assist and remove the markings from this picture. There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, I am going to do this in order to lead the witness a little bit and move this along.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, the road below the G on the right-hand side --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we ask for the assistance of the usher? He can use an arrow just to indicate and see. Well, I think it can be done from your computer, but also perhaps there, so that we all know what we are looking at. No, no markings at this moment, please. I just want you to use the curser in order to follow the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, please look at the road below the G on the left-hand side. Do you see that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This road?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, that one. To the left, on the leaf side of that road, is that the Senjak military barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Senjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To the left of the road, that's where Senjak should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So the wall that we saw on the film is along the left-hand side of that road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where the wall should be, here; because if you look across the wall, you see the fortress. So the wall should be here on this side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, is the burning building that we saw in the box -- the box marked G on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are two boxes marked G at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Misetic, at the right-hand side, could we ask the witness to point with the cursor where he thinks Mr. Misetic is referring to. Mr. Misetic, you would then confirm that he's right or wrong. Could you just use the cursor and move it to the area marked G where you say the house or at least the structure was burning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the first time I said that it appeared to me, when I looked at this video again, that this was the area, in here; but I cannot really be very precise, so that would be a rough estimate. It might be here. After we were able to look at the wall from which you can see the fortress, and after your correct conclusion that this was a building that is outside of Senjak, and on the first recording you can see that this might correspond to this larger rectangle marked G.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness is pointing with the cursor now to the rectangular structure marked G, but the right [Realtime transcript read in error "left"] one, not the left one. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can you point, Witness 6 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I have the correct the transcript. If you would read at page 53, line 3, you see that it's not reflected properly. The witness pointed at the rectangular structure marked G, but the right hand one, not the left hand one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I could ask for your indulgence to take him back to the video scene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine, by I just want to correct the apparent mistake in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, you see from the camera -- do you see a fire burning there? Can you identify on the map --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- where you see --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to admit that now I find myself in an uncomfortable situation. Based on my recollection, I cannot indicate whether it is one rectangle or the other. You're asking too much from me if you're asking me now to decide. I went to this part of the town rarely. It is in that part of the town; but whether it is on one side or the other, it could be either one of those rectangles. I cannot really be more specific than that. After all, I don't think that it should be all that important, unless you're saying that this is a depot that was set on fire here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness 6. We're going to go now next to the mark you made at point H yesterday on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, have we done with G?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, we have, Your Honour. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that, since the witness finally testified that he couldn't identify either box G to the right or box G to the left to be the location where the burning structure is, it finds itself that we forget about the markings, and are there any objections against the admission into evidence of the photograph with the two boxes marked G on it, although not by the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The unmarked version of that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then that's admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, this fire, how far is it from the army hall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we say that this is the railway station, the big building that you can see here, then this would be about a hundred metres away from the army -- from the army hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, I need to clarify something, and I'm reminded to clarify something for the Trial Chamber. Are you aware of where the headquarters of the Main Staff was in Knin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was in the rectangle that we had looked at earlier on that image that we were talking about. That's where the headquarters was. And as far as I can see, it is outside of the rectangle, closer to the fortress.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: When we use the term "army hall," do you agree that the army hall and the headquarters of the Main Staff were not the same building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is the same. I assume that it actually is the same building. The army hall was located at the same place where the headquarters was. There were two buildings, one next to the other. I didn't really have any contacts with them, so I don't know what building was used for what purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, if you elicit evidence from the witness about D rectangle, then I can choose out of five or six, I'm afraid. So would you please be more precise. How do we ask the witness further to perhaps what he --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What he means by rectangle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Or showing the picture on which most likely you will fine the rectangle he might be referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will do that, Your Honour. Yes, Your Honour. Your Honour, if I could ask Madam Registrar to take us to D18, marked for identification, I think it's page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, when you referenced a rectangle in your last answer, is this the rectangle you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's the rectangle, and now I can show you. If you have technical capabilities for that, I can indicate. This is the building. These are the two buildings that you're talking about, the two buildings where the army hall was in Knin, two buildings within this box or rectangle. The picture of the fire that you just showed me, that would be somewhere here at the very edge of this box, in the direction of the Knin fortress. So these are the three points that I marked here. So here, in the foreground, you have the army hall, which is here; and the image that we've just seen would be somewhere here. This is where the building that was hit and that was on fire is located.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, we need to be more precise for the Trial Chamber. So if you could use --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I propose numbers, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- to identify the buildings that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you like to add anything or not, because otherwise we can deal with it in a quicker way; that is, that the two blue markings most to the right are the buildings the witness referred to, whereas the last reference he made was to the marking at the very edge to the left in the area where we find trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. That would be fine, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All right. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, may I take it that the marked version of this page needs another exhibits number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It will be D20, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D20. Thank you. That's the marked page of the series of photographs we've seen before. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6, you also identified, on the map yesterday, the location of your apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if the Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If we are talking about apartments and where the witness lived, then we have to go in --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Private session would be the best, please, and the picture's not to be shown on the screen for the public. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness 6 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are we still in private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Let me just have a look. We are in open session now; but if you would need to remain in private session, we'll just return into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I would like to ask you to do that, because there might be a possibility --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm going back to your statement in which you say that that morning you woke with sounds of heavy shelling. You went to a cellar nearby and then to a village nearby, which we shall not be mentioning. When you left your flat, did you take any important belongings with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't take anything with me, not even my diploma, and this is something that I pointed out in my statement. I brought some wine and some brandy. So talking about important belongings, we can leave it at wine and brandy. I didn't take anything because I didn't think at the time that I was leaving forever. I thought I was going somewhere else for a day or two, until the whole thing blew over, allowing me to go back; not just me, most of those who were on their way at the time, and everybody did the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But you did go back to your flat, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I went back to fetch the car, I went back to the flat, and I gathered the things that I told you about, after which I drove back to this village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And then you were going to roast a lamb once back in the village; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It seemed like the cleverest thing to do at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: All in the midst of the heavy shelling that you spoke about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shelling was taking a place at a distance of 30 or 40 kilometres from that village. We were expecting at the time that it would come to a halt at any moment, that there would be a compromise, that an agreement would be reached. Unfortunately, that was not the case. A column headed out of my village, and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mikulicic. Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Cayley, who is counsel for Mr. Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Witness 6, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I think we need to go into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness 6, in your statement, you say that - and I'm referring to paragraph 16 - "The shells fell everywhere. It did not seem that they had certain targets. The purpose seemed to be to scare people and make them leave." Now, we went through a couple of locations which you marked on a photograph of damaged buildings and plume of smoke. On the basis of what we heard during the cross-examination, the plumes of smoke - of course, we have seen several ones - but at some occasions might have been seven times the same plume of smoke; whereas, some of the buildings - at least that is what the Defence tried to establish - at first sight seemed to be sometimes in the vicinity of objects that one could imagine that they could be considered military targets such as barracks. Now, having gone through these details, would you still say that it did not seem that they had certain targets, or would you say at this moment, in view of the details we have just discussed, at least part or all of the shelling I saw fell at least in vicinity of the specific objects which might have been chosen as targets? I'd like to have your comments on the rather pertinent, rather absolute way in which you phrased, "It did not seem that they had certain targets. The purpose seemed to scare people and make them leave." Could you please comment on it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-006 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I can. What we were able to see in this film, Your Honour, these are locations that were recorded by this camera at that given time, but this shelling did not last only four the time while they recorded this. It lasted until the afternoon, while I was in Knin. I can say that in the morning, before the dawn broke, that sounds of shells falling, the sounds of shelling, came from various directions. I couldn't ascertain the directions, whether the buildings targeted were military facilities, but I can say that the building close to me was hit -- was among the first buildings to be hit. On the other hand, in the morning hours, as I was to learn later, a woman was killed in a building on the other side of the town. That's Ana Tomic, a refugee from Split, a ballet dancer, a well-known person in Knin. Her building was close to the Catholic church of St. Anthony in Knin. On the other hand, when I was in a position to observe what was happening in the town, that was at a later time around noon, I was able to see what was depicted in the film; not only from those locations, but also from some other positions, one could perceive, one could see that buildings had been hit. I explained that, that as I moved through the town, that I was able to see that some buildings had been hit. So what we saw there, that would be the army hall, I assumed that the fire was concentrated in that area, or rather, at the Senjak area. Again, that was probably under heavily shelling. We didn't see the northern barracks. It probably was also shelled quite heavily and there were casualties there. This barracks is part of the town. People got killed there, and also the police station. We're talking about facilities that are inside the town itself. It's not a large town. Those facilities are concentrated in the town itself; and if you want to hit those facilities, you have to be really very accurate. I simply have to say that this was the impression that I was left with. To this day, I cannot get rid of this fear of the shelling that you have inside you. So this is the context in which I can confirm that, in addition to the facilities and buildings that we saw, that other facilities and other buildings were hit. I could not now ascertain the number of shells that hit that area, hundreds, thousands. I really can only estimate here. We didn't count them, but probably there is an expert who will be able to explain that. I'm sure that you will have a more reliable witness here who will be able to ascertain all the other locations where the shells hit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understand that what you say is what we saw on this -- on this video footage does not give the complete, picture as I saw it that day, because it's limited in time. Thank you for that answer. I have no further questions for you. Does this question raise any further issues?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, Mr. Mikulicic, not. Then this had concludes your evidence. I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and to answer the questions of both parties and of this Bench, and I wish you a safe trip home again. We stand --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- adjourned until tomorrow, Wednesday, the 9th of April, 9.00, same courtroom.
